edges.description: Mutant subunits suppress the channel activity and trafficking of co-expressed wild-type connexin 26.
edges.target: Loss of Connexin 26 Gap Junction Coupling

edges.description: Skin-associated mutant subunits interact directly with wild-type connexin 43 and inhibit its channels, in parallel with (not downstream of) the loss of connexin 26 coupling; deafness-only mutants suppress connexin 26 but spare connexin 43.
In the cochlea, loss of supporting-cell gap junction coupling impairs potassium handling around the sensory hair cells; inferred from the R75W dominant-negative mouse.
edges.source: Loss of Connexin 26 Gap Junction Coupling
edges.target: Impaired Potassium Recycling by Organ of Corti Supporting Cells

edges.description: Disturbed epidermal gap junction communication is thought to perturb keratinocyte growth and differentiation and so produce palmoplantar hyperkeratosis; the intermediate steps are not established.
Disturbed cortilymph homeostasis degrades the organ of Corti.
edges.source: Impaired Potassium Recycling by Organ of Corti Supporting Cells

edges.description: Loss of sensory hair cells produces sensorineural hearing loss.
Reproduces supporting-cell deformity, failure of the tunnel of Corti and hair-cell degeneration with severe to profound deafness.
edges.limitations: The mouse is a model of the cochlear arm only; it is described as non-syndromic, so it does not model the keratoderma. Transgene overexpression does not reproduce the human heterozygous dosage, and the potassium mechanism is the authors' inference (endocochlear potential was normal).

edges.description: AAV-delivered adenine base editing of R75W restores gap junction plaques in cochlear supporting cells, a preclinical correction of the lesion.
edges.limitations: The quoted result is restored gap junction plaque structure, not shown here to restore coupling or hearing; preclinical, untested in humans, and does not address the skin.
edges.source: CX26 R75W transgenic mouse treated with AAV base editing
edges.target: Loss of Connexin 26 Gap Junction Coupling

nodes.id: CX26 R75W transgenic mouse treated with AAV base editing

nodes.description: Cochlear implantation with hearing rehabilitation restores auditory input. The disease-specific evidence is a single R75W case report; the rationale that GJB2 pathology spares the cochlear neurons the implant stimulates comes from nonsyndromic GJB2 deafness.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary palmoplantar keratoderma and deafness resulting from genetic mutation of Connexin 26.
evidence.snippet: Cochlear implantation was done to modify hearing loss of the patient and further hearing rehabilitation had been provided by the hearing support service team in hospital

nodes.description: A heterozygous GJB2 missense variant (G59A, R75W/R75Q, H73R, deletion of E42) produces a connexin 26 subunit that cannot form functional gap junction channels and interferes with wild-type subunits.

evidence.reference_title: A connexin 26 mutation causes a syndrome of sensorineural hearing loss and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis (MIM 148350).
evidence.snippet: We report a missense mutation in the connexin 26 gene (GJB2) in a family with an autosomal dominant syndrome of hearing loss and hyperkeratosis

evidence.reference_title: GJB2-Related Hearing Loss: Genotype-Phenotype Correlations, Natural History, and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies.
evidence.snippet: A subset of GJB2 missense variants cause autosomal dominant HL through dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanisms

meta.association: Heterozygous dominant-negative missense variants in connexin 26.

evidence.reference_title: AAV-mediated base editing restores cochlear gap junction in GJB2 dominant-negative mutation-associated syndromic hearing loss model.
evidence.snippet: Dominant-negative mutations of GJB2, such as R75W, cause syndromic hearing loss and palmoplantar keratoderma

evidence.reference_title: Functional defects of Cx26 resulting from a heterozygous missense mutation in a family with dominant deaf-mutism and palmoplantar keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: We have observed a similar phenotype in an Egyptian family that segregated with a heterozygous missense mutation of GJB2, leading to a non-conservative amino acid substitution (R75W)

nodes.description: Supporting cells of the organ of Corti fail to clear potassium from the cortilymph around the sensory hair cells. In the dominant-negative mouse the endolymph potential stays normal, so the defect is local to the organ of Corti rather than to endolymph generation; the authors extend this to humans only as probable.
nodes.id: Impaired Potassium Recycling by Organ of Corti Supporting Cells

evidence.reference_title: Transgenic expression of a dominant-negative connexin26 causes degeneration of the organ of Corti and non-syndromic deafness.
evidence.snippet: the GJB2 mutation disturbs homeostasis of cortilymph, an extracellular space surrounding the sensory hair cells, due to impaired K(+) transport by supporting cells, resulting in degradation of the organ of Corti

nodes.description: Gap junctional intercellular communication through connexin 26 channels is lost, both because mutant subunits are non-functional and because they impair trafficking of wild-type connexin 26 to the plasma membrane.
nodes.id: Loss of Connexin 26 Gap Junction Coupling

nodes.description: Mutant connexin 26 subunits interact with connexin 43 in keratinocytes and suppress its channel function. This is proposed as the principal reason dominant GJB2 variants produce a skin phenotype.

evidence.snippet: the principal mechanism for manifestation of dominant GJB2 mutations in the skin is their dominant interference with the function of wtCx43
